meaning: A complete group returning from exile
description: 160 appears in the Bible in Ezra 8:10, where it is mentioned that 160 men from the descendants of Shelomith joined Ezra on the return journey from Babylon to Jerusalem. The number can be understood as 10 × 16, where ten symbolizes completeness and sixteen (4 × 4) may be linked to an intensified earthly wholeness. In this context, the 160 men represent a complete group that took part in the great restoration of the Jewish community in the promised land. Although the number 160 does not have a broad independent symbolic tradition in Jewish or Christian theology, it gains its meaning through the context: faithfulness, belonging, and participation in God’s redemptive-historical plan for return from exile.

versions.meaning: The number 160 has no well-established or known symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 160 is not a number that appears with special symbolic weight in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) in a way that has gained broad recognition. It can be decomposed mathematically (for example, 10 × 16 or 8 × 20), but none of these combinations are assigned a specific theological meaning tied specifically to 160. Some may attempt to derive meaning through gematria by finding Hebrew words with this numerical value, but this does not yield any generally accepted symbolic interpretation.

footnotes.text: In Ezra 8, several family groups are listed along with their respective numbers of men who went up with Ezra from Babylon. These figures serve as documentation that the return was organized and complete, in accordance with God's will.
